page.layout: One column of running text. Marginal notes in the left margin (year numbers 913 and 1169, both doubtful). A short fragment at the right margin beside the line "volâ". Below the text, two citation lines, one at left and one at centre. Catchword at right foot.

main_text.p: hoc si mihi abstuleris, patria ipsa mihi immortale pro hoc reponet. Maximus serm.31.

Sic & DERCYLLIDÆS Lacedæmonius, à Spartano populo missus ad Pyrrhum Regem legatus: cum eum Pyrrhus gravibus verbis urgeret, ut Lacedæmonii Cleonymum Regem, quem expulerant, in regnum recipe-rent: nulla illius dignitatis ratione habita, respondit: Si deus es; nobis, qui justam causam fovemus, minimè ti-mendus es: sin homo, tantopere nobis à te formidandum non est. Plutarchus in Laconicis.

GERMANORUM legatos gladium aliquando Alexandro Magno obtulisse, memorat Aventinus lib.1. Annal. Bojorum: quos convivio adhibitos, cum Alexander, Quidnam maximè timerent? (ratus, Sed dictu-ros) interrogaret: Nihil aliud, Rex praestantissime, responderunt; quàm ne cœlum in nos ruat.

M. Crassum, teste Plutarcho in ejus vita, contra Parthos proficiscentem, adierunt Arsacis legati hujusmodi oratione: 913.Si missus à populo Romano exercitus esset; gesturum ipsum implacabile & inexpugnabile bellum: sin patria invita, privati quaestus gratia Crassus arma Parthis intulisset, & urbes occupasset; Arsacem moderatè acturum, & Crassi senectutis miserturum, populoq; Romano milites, quos obsessos tenebat potius, quàm in praesidiis locatos, remissurum. Ad ea Crasso jactante, Seleuciae se responsum darunt [?]: ex legatis VAGISES, qui cæteros ætate anteibat, ridens, manus supinæ ostensa volâ: Hinc prius (inquit) pili Crasse exorientur, quàm tu aspicias Seleuciam.

Non dissimili fere modo CARBICUS Comes Polonus, legatus ad [illegible, ~6 letters] V. Imperatorem, cum Caesar ingentem thesaurum monstraret, subjiciens Polonos perdomabit: 1169.annulo, quem digito gerebat, in thesaurum projecto: Aurum (dixit) adjiciamus auro: [illegible, ~4 letters]ram scilicet Caesaris jactantiam notans. Hoc scomma Caesar gratias agendo elusit, Habdanci [?] inquiens lingua Germanica. Inde familiæ nomen mansit, ut

page.notes: The right margin fragment "ensa" beside "volâ" is probably the end of a word split across the line ("ostensa") and is not separate text. The left-margin year numbers 913 and 1169 are doubtful. "Dercyllidæs" is set in small capitals. The word after "Aurum (dixit)" and the Emperor's name are illegible or doubtful. "praestantissime" is read from a ligature and is doubtful. "darunt" is doubtful. "Habdanci" in the body is partly black letter and doubtful. The bottom-right "Ex h" is doubtful as a signature. Two citations appear at the foot and are kept as separate notes. The catchword "ut" is at the right foot.
